title: Intermittent Egress Burst Tolerance and Operator Fallback — Private/VPC PRD
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD describing requirements and acceptance criteria for supporting short-duration, scheduled or on-demand egress bursts in Private/VPC deployments as a safe, auditable mechanism for artifact synchronization, KMS rotation, and emergency package pulls while preserving air-gapped guarantees and operator rollback semantics.
background: Customers operating in sealed or highly restricted VPCs frequently require occasional outbound connectivity for critical maintenance (image syncs, KMS rotations, CVE fixes). Existing private-deploy flows expect either continuous egress or fully offline provisioning. This PRD defines a controlled egress-burst mechanism (timeboxed, authenticated, auditable) and the operator fallback behaviors that must be supported if bursts fail or are incomplete.
goals: Provide a deterministic, auditable egress-burst protocol that operators can trigger or schedule with minimal blast radius
Ensure artifact integrity and provenance during bursts (signed manifests, checksums, reproducible mirrors)
Define safe operator fallback and rollback behaviors for partial syncs or failed artifact application
Preserve airgap compatibility: support zero-trust verification so egress windows do not create persistent external trust dependencies
Offer telemetry and SLOs to detect burst failures, partial synchronizations, and automatic remediation guidance
non_goals: Designing a full asynchronous multi-region mirror protocol (out of scope; scope limited to single-customer burst flows)
Providing non-auditable ad-hoc outbound tunnels bypassing operator controls
Supporting long-running or continuous egress for day-to-day operations
constraints: Network operators may only open egress for a bounded window (configurable; default 15 minutes)
All artifacts must be signed and verifiable locally using pre-provisioned signing keys or root-of-trust certificates
Operator actions must be reversible where possible; irreversible schema changes require explicit manual approval steps
Bucketed bandwidth quotas and per-burst token allowance enforced by customer operator and the operator agent
proposed_solution_summary: Introduce a burst-egress orchestration flow in the private operator that: 1) validates a scheduled or operator-initiated burst request, 2) opens a timebound egress channel via the operator-configured egress-proxy, 3) prefetches an artifact manifest, 4) verifies signatures/checksums locally, 5) applies artifacts in an idempotent staged fashion with pre/post checks, 6) if failures occur, triggers an automated fallback plan (quarantine artifacts, roll back applied components, escalate to operator).
detailed_requirements: Burst lifecycle: request -> authenticate -> open egress -> fetch manifest -> fetch artifacts -> verify -> staged-apply -> validate -> close egress -> archive audit
Request authorization: bursts require at least two operator approvals OR an approved schedule tied to an operator role (configurable RBAC)
Timebox enforcement: operator agent must strictly enforce configured window; any downloads beyond the window must be terminated and retried under a new request
Manifest format: JSON manifest with artifact list, semver, SHA256 checksums, signature (detached), and optional migration steps. Manifest must be verifiable with locally cached root-of-trust certs
Transport: support HTTPS and signed OCI-style pulls; optionally support scp/rsync for airgapped customers that provide push endpoints
Resumable transfers: artifact downloads should support chunked/resumable semantics and a deterministic retry policy limited to the burst window
Atomic application: artifacts applied in a two-stage model (stage -> validate -> promote) to enable rollback to last known-good state
KMS rotation within burst: support pre-sequenced key rotations where new keys are pre-provisioned in operator and rotation handshake occurs only after artifact verification

Telemetry and audit: every burst must produce an immutable audit record (start/end timestamps, operator IDs, manifest hash, artifact checksums, bytes transferred, outcome, errors) exported to customer telemetry sinks and stored locally

Fallback modes: on partial failure the operator agent should (a) stop further application, (b) quarantine incomplete artifacts, (c) attempt automated revert of staged changes, (d) open an incident ticket template and optionally re-open a single-purpose egress window for emergency fixes
Offline compensation: support pre-seeding of artifact caches via physical media or operator-pushed bundle if bursts are rejected or networks blocked
acceptance_criteria: AC1: An operator can schedule and authorize a 15-minute egress burst with two operator approvals and the system records the approval chain
AC2: During a burst, the operator agent fetches a signed manifest, verifies signatures against the local root-of-trust, and rejects manifests with missing or invalid signatures
AC3: Artifact downloads must complete within the configured window or be cleanly terminated; partial downloads produce a quarantine state and do not corrupt existing runtime state
AC4: Staged-apply mechanism guarantees that if validation fails after stage, the system reverts to previous running state within 3 minutes and reports the revert action in audit logs

AC5: KMS key rotation flow performed during a scheduled burst completes only after artifact verification and logs key-change events; any failure triggers key rollback to previous key and signals an immediate alert
AC6: Audit record shipped to configured telemetry sink within 5 minutes of burst close and contains manifest hash, operator IDs, bytes transferred, and final status

AC7: If burst window is prematurely closed (network or operator), operator can re-open a single-purpose emergency burst with escalated authorization and the system performs safety checks before resuming
AC8: End-to-end egress burst test in CI harness simulating network drop results in deterministic fallback actions and passes automated verifications for at least 3 simulated failure modes
AC9: Documentation and on-call runbook published and linked from Console with step-by-step operator procedures and checklist
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest verification, signature validation, and chunked download logic
Integration test: simulate scheduled burst against a staging mirror, verify staged-apply then promote
Chaos test: interrupt network mid-download and assert quarantine + revert behavior
KMS rotation test: pre-provision new keys, perform rotation during burst, validate rotation telemetry and rollback on failure
End-to-end CI job that runs weekly to exercise the burst flow against a closed-network emulator
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind operator flag and customer opt-in
Beta with three pilot customers who consent to limited telemetry and sign-off
Monitor pilot for 4 weeks; collect failure modes and adjust timebox defaults
Gradual rollout to general availability once SLOs for success/rollback are met
operational_checklist: Pre-burst: confirm root-of-trust cert present and not expired
Pre-burst: ensure mirror endpoints are reachable from test harness
During burst: operator monitors bytes transferred and manifest verification status in Console stream
Post-burst: verify audit record archived and telemetry shows no partial-apply remaining
Failure: follow runbook to open emergency burst or apply physical-media fallback
telemetry_and_observability: Real-time burst stream: per-burst progress (manifest hash, artifact count, bytes/sec)
Dashboard: historical burst success rate, mean bytes transferred, mean revert time
Trace links: operator approval chain and PR/Change links for applied artifacts
security_considerations: Manifest and artifacts must be signed with customer-owned keys; Redwood operator will not accept unsigned artifacts
Operator approvals are RBAC enforced and audit logged; integration with SSO/SAML required for pilot
Burst windows are ephemeral and no persistent outbound tunnels created; egress proxies must be ephemeral and auditable
KMS rotations must be atomic from the perspective of the runtime and must not leave partial key states
